SVS Medical College has taught MBBS in Mahabubnagar since 1999. The course follows the NMC’s competency-based curriculum, with clinical learning in the SVS Teaching Hospital on the same campus.

Since
1999
Annual MBBS intake
150 seats
Affiliated to
KNRUHS, Warangal
Teaching hospital
1,043 beds

Our journey

  1. 1999

    The Government of India grants the Letter of Permission for 100 MBBS seats. The degree is affiliated to Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences, Vijayawada.

  2. 2013

    Continuation of recognition for 100 MBBS seats.

  3. 2013–14

    Permission to increase the annual intake from 100 to 150 seats.

  4. 2018

    The Central Government recognises the increased intake of 150 seats (February).

  5. Today

    Affiliated to Kaloji Narayana Rao University of Health Sciences (KNRUHS), Warangal.

The doctor you’ll become

The course prepares an Indian Medical Graduate to serve as a physician of first contact.

  • Clinician

    Preventive, promotive, curative, palliative and holistic care, given with compassion.

  • Leader and team member

    Coordinates health activities in primary and secondary care settings.

  • Communicator

    Speaks with patients, families, colleagues and communities with empathy.

  • Lifelong learner

    Keeps assessing and building clinical knowledge and procedural skills.

  • Professional

    Practises ethically, stays accountable and follows statutory codes of conduct.

  • Critical thinker and researcher

    Uses evidence-based medicine and contributes to scientific enquiry.

How the course works

  1. Foundation course

    Orientation, basic first aid and life support, professional development, language and computer skills, and community visits.

  2. Subjects and practicals

    Subject teaching with practical work, and skills-lab practice on mannequins and task trainers before patient contact.

  3. Clinical postings

    Learning at the bedside in the teaching hospital, with communication, ethics and patient dignity throughout.

  4. Community learning

    The Family Adoption Programme follows households through repeated visits, linked to the rural and urban health centres.

  5. Electives and assessment

    Electives, internal assessment and university examinations, followed by the Compulsory Rotating Medical Internship (CRMI).

Attendance and progression rules

RequirementMinimum
Theory attendance, each subject and phase75%
Practical or clinical attendance80%
AETCOM attendance75%
Family Adoption Programme field visits80%
Electives75%
Internal assessment, theory and practical combined50% (at least 40% in each)
Moving to Phase IIAll Phase I subjects passed
Phase I attemptsUp to 4, within 4 years
Completing MBBS, including CRMIWithin 10 years of admission

Students who miss the attendance or internal assessment minimums can’t sit the regular university examination. Remedial measures may restore eligibility for the supplementary examination, so confirm the rules for your batch with the academic office.
